> 為學日益，為道日損。損之又損，以至於無為.

Chapter 47 was about the eye: the more you look, the more fragmented it gets.

Chapter 48 is about adding and subtracting — the only chapter that sets two paths side by side on one table.

One is called 為學: every day, more.
One is called 為道: every day, less.

And the harshest thing in the chapter hides in the most ordinary character.

## 取 is to cut off an ear

取: 捕取也, from 又 (hand) and 耳 (ear). It is the battlefield gesture — cutting off the enemy's left ear to carry back for the count.

So 取天下 is not "win the world" in any neutral sense. Its original sense is a bleeding action: taking something by removing a piece of it.

Which is why the line lands where it does: 取天下常以无事 — you cannot take the world by cutting ears off it.

## 日益: what actually grows

為學日益 — the daily increase in learning.

The chapter does not say the increase is knowledge. It says what increases is 界: boundaries. Each thing learned well enough to be used becomes a distinction, and each distinction is an edge that now has to be maintained.

Learning that produces usable distinctions is necessary. The problem is that the count of edges grows without limit, and so does the maintenance.

## 日損: what is being removed

為道日損 — the daily decrease in the way.

損 removes 附著 — the attachments, the things stuck onto what you know. Not the knowledge; the sediment around it.

This distinction is what keeps the chapter from being anti-intellectual. Nothing about knowing is being reduced. What is being reduced is the weight that accumulated around the knowing: the position it gave you, the identity it supported, the arguments it required.

## 損之又損，以至於無為

Reduce, and reduce again, until you arrive at non-forcing.

The repetition is the instruction: it is not one subtraction. It is a movement that continues, and 至 is the arrival — you don't decide to be 無為; you arrive there when there is nothing left to remove.

Which means 無為 is not a technique one adopts. It is what remains.

## 無為而無不為

Non-forcing, and nothing is left undone.

The pairing is not a claim about effectiveness. It is the observation that what was preventing completion was the forcing — nothing else was in the way.

## 及其有事，不足以取天下

Once there is 事 — once there are affairs you are managing, things you are making happen — you no longer have enough to take the world.

不足 is a capacity statement: the capacity got spent on the managing.

## What the two paths share

Both are daily. Neither is a decision made once.

That is the practical core. 為學 and 為道 are not two schools; they are two directions of the same daily movement, and a person is always doing some of both.

The question is only which one is dominant — and whether the subtracting is keeping up with the adding.

## A test

Take the last thing you learned seriously. Then ask: did it add an edge, or did it remove one? Most learning adds. The rare kind removes — it makes something you were defending unnecessary.
